description: Mobile app security challenge registry for mobsec-ctf-lab. Consumed by scripts/provision.py to create challenges in CTFd. Modules follow the course AGENTS.md: Android Architecture (Set 1), Static Analysis (Set 2), Dynamic Analysis (Set 3). Challenge id/name/value/difficulty/flag/hints.

challenges.name: Arch: Manifest Export Misconfiguration (L1)
challenges.description:
Download and decompile the GlowMart Mobile APK (GlowMartMobile.apk) from the app store (see the Module 1 brief).

Open the decompiled AndroidManifest.xml with jadx or apktool. One component is exported without a good reason and carries a flag in its metadata.

Find the flag and submit it inside flag{...}.
hints: Look for an <activity> with android:exported="true" that has no intent-filter.
Flags hidden in manifest components often live in <meta-data> values.
Decompile with: jadx GlowMartMobile.apk   (or: apktool d GlowMartMobile.apk).

challenges.name: Arch: Exported Activity Intent-Extra Leak (L1)
challenges.description:
This challenge is about exported Activities and their Intent contracts.

GlowMart Mobile contains an exported debug activity that reveals a secret flag — but only when the correct Intent extra is supplied.

Decompile the app to discover the Activity name, the extra key it reads, and the magic value it expects, then launch it with adb to reveal the flag (or read its value directly).

Example: adb shell am start -n com.glowmart.mobile/.DebugLeakActivity --es <key> <value>
hints: Search the decompiled source for getIntent().getStringExtra(...).
The Activity compares the extra against a static constant — 'auth_override' = 'grant'.
The revealed flag is also stored in res/values/strings.xml.

challenges.name: Arch: Flag Hidden in Resources (L1)
challenges.description:
Static resources often contain secrets that developers forget about.

In GlowMart Mobile, a flag is hidden in one of the packaged resource files (strings.xml, assets, or res/raw).

Decompile the APK and look through the resource files. jadx shows res/raw and assets automatically; apktool exposes the raw layout.
hints: Check assets/ first and then res/raw/.
A file named secret_codebook.json in res/raw contains an embedded secret.
Also decompile the APK's strings.xml — an unused string may be a red herring.

challenges.name: Arch: Unprotected Content Provider (L2)
challenges.description:
Content Providers control access to app data. An exported provider without permission checks lets any app (or adb) read it.

GlowMart Mobile defines an exported ContentProvider at authority com.glowmart.mobile.secrets.

Query it to extract the flag. From adb:

adb shell content query --uri content://com.glowmart.mobile.secrets/flag
hints: The provider is declared in AndroidManifest.xml with android:exported="true".
Query the authority with the path segment 'flag'.
Try: adb shell content query --uri content://com.glowmart.mobile.secrets/flag

challenges.name: Static: Hardcoded API Key (L2)
challenges.description:
Reverse the app's authentication layer.

GlowMart Mobile embeds an API key directly in its Java sources. Decompile the app and locate the class that supplies authentication tokens; the key is stored as a constant.

j adx-gui makes source navigation easy; apktool shows the smali (more painful but exact).
hints: Search the decompiled sources for 'API_KEY' or 'api_key'.
The class AuthTokenProvider exposes a public static final String.
Hardcoded secrets in source = CWE-798.

challenges.name: Static: Weakly Encoded Flag (L2)
challenges.description:
Not all 'encryption' is encryption.

GlowMart Mobile stores a private note as a plaintext-looking constant that is only encoded, not encrypted.

Find the encoded constant in the decompiled sources and decode it manually. CyberChef can decode Base64 in a single step.
hints: Look in the Strings class for a Base64-encoded constant.
Copy the constant into CyberChef → From Base64.
If you find an XOR step, the key is a single low byte (try 0x2A or brute force 0x00-0xFF).

challenges.name: Static: Insecure Crypto - Static AES Key (L2)
challenges.description:
Cryptography is only as good as its key management.

GlowMart Mobile decrypts a secret with AES-128-ECB using a hardcoded key and no IV.

Decompile the CryptoBox class, note the algorithm ('AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding'), extract the key and the base64 ciphertext, and decrypt it. CyberChef (AES Decrypt → ECB) works perfectly.
hints: Constant-time key: a 16-byte ASCII string, not random-looking.
ECB mode: no IV needed, no mode dependencies.
Use AES-128, key in UTF-8, PKCS7 padding, output raw → the flag is the plaintext.

challenges.name: Static: MobSF Flagged Secret (L2)
challenges.description:
Automated scanners make secrets easy to find.

Run the APK through MobSF (static scan). One of the flagged findings contains a live flag — a hardcoded secret MobSF reports as a vulnerability.

(MobSF can be run locally via Docker; a pre-baked MobSF report is included in the app store if the scanner is unavailable.)
hints: MobSF's 'Hardcoded Secrets' / 'Embedded Credentials' section lists values found in code and resources.
The secret also sits in res/values/secrets.xml under the name api_secret_key.
Scan endpoint: static scan the uploaded GlowMartMobile.apk.

challenges.name: Static: Native Library String (L3 / stretch)
challenges.description:
Native code is a favorite hiding place for secrets.

GlowMart Mobile loads a small shared library (libglowmart.so). Extract the native library from the APK (unzip the jniLibs/lib/<abi>/libglowmart.so) and run strings(1) on it.

A strings(1) dump is also available in the app store if you do not want to unzip.
hints: unzip GlowMartMobile.apk 'lib/*/libglowmart.so' then: strings libglowmart.so | grep -i flag
The flag is embedded as an ordinary C string in the shared library.
The native source is at targets/app/app/src/main/cpp/glowlib.c.

challenges.name: Dynamic: SSL Pinning Bypass (L3)
challenges.description:
The app talks to its backend over TLS with certificate pinning.

Install the APK on an emulator, start Burp Suite or mitmproxy as your interception proxy, and try to read the app's /api/v1/mobile/banner call. Certificate pinning will block it.

Bypass the pinning with a Frida hook (overriding PinnedApiClient.checkServerTrusted) and intercept the call to obtain the flag.

The backend HTTPS endpoint is https://10.0.2.2:3443 (emulator) / https://127.0.0.1:3443 (host).
hints: Hook com.glowmart.mobile.PinnedApiClient and neuter its pin check (return without throwing).
Objection: android sslpinning disable  works on many implementations.
Alternatively hook javax.net.ssl.SSLContext.init to accept the proxy CA.

challenges.name: Dynamic: Root Detection Bypass (L3)
challenges.description:
A 'vault' screen in GlowMart Mobile refuses to open on rooted devices.

Run the app on a rooted emulator and launch the vault (MainActivity → 'Open vault', or adb shell am start -n com.glowmart.mobile/.VaultActivity). It will report root detected and stay locked.

Bypass the RootCheck.isDeviceRooted() check with Frida so the vault unlocks, then read the flag.
hints: Frida: Java.perform → hook com.glowmart.mobile.RootCheck.isDeviceRooted and return false.
The vault reveals the flag when isDeviceRooted() returns false.
On a non-rooted emulator the vault opens directly — that is also the expected runtime result.

challenges.name: Dynamic: Frida Runtime-Decrypt Dump (L3)
challenges.description:
Some secrets only exist at run time.

GlowMart Mobile decrypts a blob at run time with a caller-supplied argument (userId). Decode CryptoBox-adjacent class Vault: its getDecryptedSecret(int userId) returns the decrypted secret in memory.

Use Frida to hook Vault.getDecryptedSecret, call it with the correct userId (4242), and dump the return value.
hints: Hook: Java.perform → var Vault = Java.use('com.glowmart.mobile.Vault'); console.log(Vault.getDecryptedSecret(4242));
The userId used by the app's license check is 4242.
Static XOR decoding is possible too: the blob is base64, key = userId & 0xFF.

challenges.name: Dynamic: Logcat Debug Leak (L2)
challenges.description:
Debug logging leaks secrets into a place everyone can read.

Launch GlowMart Mobile on the emulator and watch logcat while the MainActivity initialises. A debug log line contains a flag.

adb logcat | grep -i flag
hints: Start logcat before launching the app: adb logcat -c && adb shell am start -n com.glowmart.mobile/.MainActivity && adb logcat -d | grep GlowMartDebug
The tag is GlowMartDebug.
Search logcat for the literal pattern flag{...}.

challenges.name: Dynamic: Local Storage Forensics (L3)
challenges.description:
Apps store state where attackers can pull it.

After using GlowMart Mobile once, pull its private data directory and inspect the SQLite database and SharedPreferences.

adb pull /data/data/com.glowmart.mobile (rooted) or adb backup / run-as extraction, then inspect glowmart.db and shared_prefs/session_data.xml for a stored flag.
hints: SQLite file: /data/data/com.glowmart.mobile/databases/glowmart.db, table 'secrets'.
SharedPreferences: /data/data/com.glowmart.mobile/shared_prefs/session_data.xml, key 'remembered_flag'.
On a non-rooted emulator: adb exec-out run-as com.glowmart.mobile cat databases/glowmart.db works for debuggable builds.
